LESS UNCERTAINTY BETWEEN HEARINGS

Spend less time working out the next step.

An inquiry brings legal duties, sensitive interactions and operational pressure together. Clear preparation helps your team spend less time reconstructing what should happen next.

Reduce avoidable rework

Find the document relevant to the current step, check procedural gaps and keep source records organised in your institution’s custody.

Keep deadlines visible

Record receipt, verified commencement, hearings, report and implementation separately. See outstanding checks and next actions while working in the guide.

Give the team greater clarity

Know what needs attention, which role should act and what to verify before the next step. A clearer process can reduce avoidable uncertainty and management effort.

See how the guide supports your CommitteeDiscuss the time-consuming steps in your process

FAIRNESS NOW. A RECORD YOU CAN EXPLAIN LATER.

Be prepared if the process is questioned.

Help your Committee check notice, participation, supporting and contrary material, and the reasons behind its decisions. These are matters to address during the inquiry—not reconstruct after a challenge.

Navigator provides procedural prompts and editable drafts. Your institution retains the signed documents, original evidence and authorised findings.

Discuss your Committee’s needs

Build around fair opportunity

  • Confirm authority and applicable rules.
  • Record actual service and response opportunities.
  • Prepare hearings, evidence and witness steps.
  • Keep findings and recommendations Committee-owned.
  • Review report, implementation and follow-up dates.

No plan guarantees an appeal outcome. Sound records support review; the law, facts and conduct of the inquiry still matter.

AVAILABLE IN THE GUIDED WORKSPACE

Relevant tools for each inquiry step.

Contextual document drafts

Start from professionally prepared, source-informed templates for intake, conciliation, notices, hearings, evidence, witnesses, report and implementation. Adapt the wording to the facts instead of drafting every document from scratch.

Dates and follow-up review

Use distinct statutory triggers and verified records. Surface due items, missing checks and responsible roles without turning reminders into legal decisions.

Local recovery and handover

Save and verify a recovery file, resume your session, and prepare a printable review sheet. Official case custody remains with your institution.

What can Navigator help us achieve?

A more structured procedural workflow, relevant drafts, visible date checks and clearer handovers. It can help reduce avoidable omissions and repeat work. Actual time and cost savings depend on your process and use; no saving figure or legal outcome is guaranteed.

Do members need to be comfortable with legal terminology?

The guide uses plain-language questions, relevant document drafts and explanations to help Committee members prepare each step. It complements orientation and capacity-building; it does not replace training, statutory eligibility, independent Committee judgment or case-specific legal advice where needed.

Does it make an inquiry appeal-proof?

No. It supports preparation for a fair process and a record your Committee can explain. It cannot prevent an appeal, validate every case fact or replace the competent authority’s assessment.

How are case records and payments handled?

Only account and plan access are held by the account service. Procedural session data stays in the browser or explicit local recovery files. Online checkout remains test-only; real online payments are disabled. Confirm any current offer and payment arrangements directly with the provider before committing.
